about.title: About NgDigest
about.lead: The Angular tech watch that aggregates the best articles, tutorials and community news — automatically curated, every 12 hours.
about.why.title: Why NgDigest?
about.why.text: Keeping up with the Angular ecosystem means juggling dozens of blogs, newsletters, and community channels. NgDigest centralises that noise into a single, scored, bilingual feed — so you spend time reading, not searching.
about.howItWorks.title: How does it work?
about.howItWorks.text: Every 12 hours, NgDigest runs an automated aggregation pipeline across three sources: SerpAPI (Google Search + News), the dev.to public API, and curated RSS feeds. Each result is deduplicated by URL and run through a relevance scoring system before being stored.
about.scoring.title: Relevance scoring
about.scoring.text: Every resource receives a score from 0 to 6 based on three signals:
about.scoring.trustedSource: +3 pts — domain is in the curated whitelist ({{ count }} trusted sources)
about.scoring.keyword: +2 pts — title contains an Angular-related keyword
about.scoring.recency: +1 pt — published within the last 7 days
about.scoring.threshold: Only resources scoring 3 or above are stored and surfaced.
about.stack.title: Tech stack
about.stack.frontend: Frontend — Angular 21 (Signals, standalone components), @ngx-translate, SCSS BEM
about.stack.backend: Backend — NestJS 11, MongoDB Atlas, Clean Architecture (DDD)
about.stack.aggregation: Aggregation — SerpAPI, dev.to API, RSS Parser
about.openSource.title: Open source
about.openSource.text: NgDigest is open source. The full source code — frontend, backend, and aggregation pipeline — is available on GitHub.

legal.privacy.title: Privacy policy
legal.privacy.introContent: NgDigest (ngdigest.co) is a personal Angular tech watch project. This policy describes the data collected during your visit, how it is used, and your rights under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
legal.privacy.trackingContent: NgDigest uses Google Analytics 4 (GA4) to measure website traffic. GA4 is only loaded after your explicit consent via the cookie banner. If you decline, no Google script is executed and no browsing data is collected. You can change your choice at any time by clearing your browser's localStorage (key: cookie_consent).
legal.privacy.localStorageContent: NgDigest uses your browser's localStorage to store your consent choice (key cookie_consent, value accepted or refused). This data stays on your device and is not transmitted to any third party. It does not expire automatically and can be deleted at any time from your browser settings.
legal.privacy.dataCollectedTitle: Data collected if GA4 consent is granted
legal.privacy.dataCollectedContent: If you accept GA4, Google Analytics collects anonymised browsing data: pages visited, session duration, device and browser type, country of origin (via IP address, anonymised by Google). No personally identifiable data is collected or stored by NgDigest.

certifications.voice.text: “Which certification do you have?” — the question comes up often in interviews. I dug in: there really is one serious Angular certification, in 3 levels, plus a few cross-cutting certs that carry weight. Here's my sorting, the levels, the prep options and the prices — verified, no sugar-coating.

certifications.disclosure.title: Prices, affiliation & CPF.
certifications.disclosure.text: Angular prices = exam-only fees (Junior $69, Mid $179); bundles with prep/bootcamp cost more, and country-based discounts (PPP) + coupons exist — confirm on certificates.dev. Transparency: our links to Certificates.dev are partner links (NgDigest may earn a commission, at no extra cost to you; it doesn't influence the selection). On CPF: US certs (Certificates.dev, IAAP, Scrum.org) aren't directly CPF-fundable — only training leading to an RNCP / Répertoire Spécifique certification (Qualiopi provider) is.

platforms.edu.title: What is umbrella employment?
platforms.edu.text: You invoice your gigs like a freelancer, but you're an employee of the umbrella company, which turns your revenue into a payslip. You keep your freedom (choosing gigs, your rate) while getting employee social protection (unemployment, pension, health cover) and simplicity (no accounting, no admin). In exchange: management fees, often 5-10% of revenue.
platforms.edu.forWho.label: Who's it for?
platforms.edu.forWho.text: Freelancers wanting to test independence without setting up a company, professionals in transition, one-off gigs, or to secure benefits (unemployment).
